objects.episodes: public 18, 39, 40 (all used to build it); eval 19 (slot 1), 38 (slot 0)
objects.evidence_in_repo: library_v2/README; work log 10-21 15:45 TRT (slab). Measured today: thickness p50 11-13 mm vs 3-5 mm (scan). Stable on its base at rest in ep18/39/40: footprint within 2 mm 41-73 cm2, COM +22 to +26 mm inside, nearest stable face 1.0-1.3 deg. Registered AUC 0.917-0.982.

scene_level_risks: Unseen undersides and edges come out rounded or open in EVERY object that rests on the table. The flatten_base fix is per object and tied to one episode's up. Today's check, at mocap ups as a diagnostic stand-in, found two new objects that cannot stand: water_pitcher (footprint 1.2 cm2, COM 2-2.5 cm outside, nearest stable face 62 deg away) and beige_cup (0.5 cm2, 29 mm outside, 46 deg away). It also found marginal ones: board 2 lying flat (+2 mm), board 1 standing (+0.4 mm), sweeper standing (about 4 mm, 4-6 deg off at other episodes' ups). A general gate is needed: for every perceived rest segment, take the hull union at our perceived up, require a stable face within 5 deg and more than 5 mm of COM margin, then run a VOC=0 drop test. Fail means fix the mesh, never train.

TSDF resolution (4 mm voxels plus Gaussian smoothing 0.8) and 'fill' closing cannot represent features under about 1 cm. Measured: board slots absent; plates 2-3x too thick (dust pan 11-13 mm vs 3-5, lid 12-13 vs 2-7, pot walls 15-20 vs 4); rack fins 2 cm low; blue cup cavity floor raised 5.5 cm; rack tower and basket floor missing; pitcher and beige-cup bottoms missing. Hand-made patches (flatten, carve) touch one symptom at a time; nothing checks the rest.

CoACD (threshold 0.05, FlashCHORD's call) inflates contacts even for perfect meshes. Scan-hull GT contact states measured today: lid in pot 7.3-7.8 mm, cup on rack 6.9-7.7 mm, sweeper in rack 9.7-12.4 mm, boards crossed 5.4-5.5 mm, nest 3.9-4.8 mm. It also fills the boards' slot of the scan's visual mesh. Carving a slot into our mesh is therefore not enough: the collision geometry must be shipped as pre-split convex <collision> pieces, which note 19 found the loader accepts and CoACD returns unchanged.

Every contact and containment state needs extra lift to clear (measured with our hulls at mocap poses): nest 9.9 cm (ep11, eval 10), cup on rack 2.3-2.6 cm (ep12/13, eval 14), lid on pot 1.7-1.9 cm (ep0/2, eval 1), sweeper in rack 2.8-3.1 cm (ep31, eval 30), pot on rack 0.8-0.9 cm (ep26/27, eval 28). Boards crossed: 16-17 cm3 / 6.5-7.3 mm overlap (ep23/24, eval 25). States present at frame 0 (lid on pot in eval 1, sweeper in rack in eval 30) pop at the evaluation reset (exact start, assist off). States at the end cannot be reached, so the policy ends 1-3 cm off (ep12 cup ends 3 cm high in rollouts).

Objects supported by or leaning on another object (cup or pot on rack, sweeper in the fins, board 1 leaning on board 2 at the end of ep24, lid on pot, nest) are explicitly skipped by contact_retarget.rest_settle ('resting on another object'). Only table support is validated. A multi-object settle is needed: a short physics settle of all objects with the hands removed, or a hull-aware projection that seats each object on its host. Check it against the reference before training.

Floating references: in the base reference (tree24s) the ep24 boards sit at a median 4.2 / 1.8 cm above the table during static frames (95 % / 77 % of them more than 5 mm). The ep12/ep27 rack sits about 1 cm high (work log), and ep12's cup tips 23 deg. rest_settle (opt-in, default off) seats them (tree24r 0.2 / 0.1 cm; tree27rs rack 0.0 cm). The settled height then depends on our mesh bottoms, which are wrong by up to 1.1 cm (board 1 protrusion).

Perception relative-pose errors create interpenetration independent of the mesh. ep31 sweeper in rack: 13.7 mm at our perception poses vs 7.6 mm at mocap poses with the same hulls. ep0 lid in pot: 15.2 mm vs 9.2 mm (known ep0 lid failure). Contact checks must run on the actual reference poses, not only on the mesh.

Slot-0 anchor sensitivity: the scorer aligns the scene once at frame 0 on the first non-symmetric object. Any reset pop of slot 0 shifts every object for the whole clip. Eval anchors at risk: 30 (sweeper inside the rack), 25 (board 1 rocking), 20 (cup held in mid-air at f0), 8 (if the pot anchors, the beige cup still falls), 15/16/28 (our broken rack).

Mass and inertia placeholders: every object is 0.3 kg, with COM and inertia from a surface-shell estimate over our mesh. That is wrong where the shell is partial (beige cup) or the interior filled (blue cup, pitcher). Mass ratios matter for tool use: sweeper on dust pan, spoon (real one far lighter: an estimate) stirring a pot or cup, scrubbing a 0.3 kg rack in eval 30.

Simulated table: the support disc is fitted to the objects' frame-0 reach. In ep27 the rack's end overhangs the disc (r 0.312 vs 0.276). Edge-dependent manipulations (ep24 slide to the edge, ep18 dust pan near the edge) need the real edge position. Friction is 1.0 everywhere, so on-table slides need lateral pushes.

Library coverage: several objects are fused from a single public episode (beige cup ep11, 137 frames; lid ep2; both boards ep23). The eval clips show other poses and other unseen faces, and no GT-free completeness check exists. The recon.json stats (unknown_share, known_frac, component count) already flag the worst: beige cup unknown_share 0.42, rack known_frac 0.44, beige 268 and lid 370 components.

Evidence gap: none of these geometric checks has been confirmed in the simulator itself. Today's numbers come from offline CoACD hulls with FlashCHORD's parameters plus my own hull geometry, not from a FlashCHORD scene build or an evaluator rollout. The next step is the VOC=0 frame_quality_probe on ep21 (pitcher), ep11 (beige cup), ep31 (sweeper in rack) and ep0/2 (lid).
notes:
Audit done read-only: no repo files changed. Scripts and logs are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-v2d-track3/8c892c5e-fd7c-57aa-abef-68d2af098e4f/scratchpad/audit/ (common.py, hulls.py + hulls/*.npz, stab.py, pairs.py, lift.py, cavity.py, slices.py, asciimap.py, asciimesh.py, pairs_*.log).

Method:
- Simulator geometry was rebuilt offline: CoACD 1.0.11 with FlashCHORD's parameters (threshold 0.05, preprocess auto), run on meshes/library_v4. The control is the public scans' visual meshes in loc/t3/mesh, without the public *_collision.glb.
- COM comes from pipeline/make_assets.surface_inertia, i.e. what our URDFs give the simulator.
- Resting 'up' directions, contact states and the alignment of our mesh to the scan use public mocap and scans. These are DIAGNOSTIC only, allowed after inference by CLAUDE.md. A pipeline gate must use our perceived up and our own reference poses. pairs.py also ran on our own perception tracks (loc/perc, refsweep perc2, made with the scan templates): every number labelled 'at our perception poses' is GT-free.
- The scan hulls come from non-manifold visual meshes, so they include CoACD voxel-remesh inflation (note 19). Treat the scan columns as an upper bound of inflation for perfect geometry.

What is measured:
- footprints, COM margins, stable faces
- cavity heights, through-holes, thickness
- overlap volume and depth
- lift needed to clear a contact state

None was run through a FlashCHORD scene build or a rollout. The severity labels are my judgement, not measurements.

Biggest new findings, not in the work log: the water_pitcher and beige_cup cannot stand; the beige cup has no bottom and is two fragments; the blue cup's cavity floor is 5.5 cm high; the rack's tower floor and basket floor are missing. The CoACD point also changes the board fix: at threshold 0.05 it fills even the scan's visual-mesh slot, so a carved slot needs pre-split collision pieces to survive.
